title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is from a typescript of P. Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques : formulaire (d'après J. Tate)', published in Modular Functions of One Variable IV, LNM 476, 1975. The section numbering (§3 2 invertible, §4 2 nilpotent with c4 invertible, §5 c4 = 0 with p = 2 or 3) and the notation (a_i, b_i, c_4, c_6, Δ, transformation (1.2) with parameters u, r, s, t, differential π) match that text. Grothendieck kept a copy in the Gauss–Manin / Cartier dossier.

**Top of page (end of §3).** Over Z[1/2], with c4 invertible, the pair (E, π) of a genus-one curve and an invertible invariant differential has a fine moduli scheme. It is Spec Z[1/2][a2, a4, a6, (a2²−3a4)^{-1}]/(a2a4−9a6), with universal curve y² = x³+a2x²+a4x+a6 and π = dx/2y. In addition, π rigidifies the curve: no nontrivial automorphism preserves π. The reason is that an automorphism fixing π has u = 1. Then fixing the normal form (no xy and y terms, plus the normalisation d6 = 0) forces r = s = t = 0.

**§4: 2 nilpotent, c4 invertible.**
- When 2 = 0, the automorphism [−1] acts on π by −1, which equals 1. So π never rigidifies a curve.
- Mod 2 one has c4 ≡ a1⁴. Hence if 2 is nilpotent and c4 is invertible, then a1 is invertible.
- After rescaling one may take a1 = 1, then a3 = a4 = 0. This gives the normal form y² + xy = x³ + a2x² + a6, with π = dx/(2y + a1x + a3) = dx/(x+2y).
- The residual changes of coordinates are r = t = 0 and u = 1+2s. Then u²a2' = a2 − s − s² and u⁶a6' = a6.
- Modulo 2: c4 = 1, c6 = 1, Δ = a6.

**§5 begins.** The page ends at the start of the supersingular case c4 = 0, p = 3.

ideas.what: Fine moduli scheme for genus-one curves with invertible invariant differential and c4 invertible over Z[1/2]; the differential rigidifies
ideas.modern_name: Moduli of elliptic curves with nonvanishing invariant differential (level structure via ω); ring of Weierstrass forms modulo the unipotent group

ideas.what: Normal form y²+xy=x³+a2x²+a6 when 2 is nilpotent and c4 invertible (ordinary in char 2), residual transformations, invariants mod 2
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass normal form for ordinary elliptic curves in characteristic 2
ideas.where_published: Deligne LNM 476; Silverman AEC Appendix A

ideas.what: In characteristic 2 the invariant differential never rigidifies, since [−1] acts trivially on ω

deep.surprise_reason: This is a copy of Deligne's published 'Formulaire' (after Tate), which Grothendieck kept in his dossier. All formulas are standard and verified correct; nothing here is original to Grothendieck or absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'mise sour forme' is a typo in the original typescript for 'mise sous forme'.
Transcription is otherwise faithful: (4.1) π = dx/(x+2y); (4.3) u²a'_2 = a_2 − s − s², u⁶a'_6 = a_6; (4.4) c_4 = 1, c_6 = 1, Δ = a_6.
